Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for the frozen product you use; the basket-loading advice here is general.
summary: Vegetarian, if the packet says so. Brush frozen vegetable dumplings with a little oil and cook them directly from frozen. No thawing or chopping is needed; follow the packet’s cooking instructions.

ingredients.note: Read the packet: vegetable fillings vary, and some contain egg, dairy or seafood. Do not swap in a frozen meat dumpling and follow these times.

ingredients.item: Neutral oil, brushed or sprayed on
ingredients.note: Helps the wrappers crisp and limits drying.

ingredients.item: Soy sauce, black vinegar and chilli oil, to dip
ingredients.note: Any two of the three make a dipping sauce. Soy sauce usually contains wheat.

method.instruction: Brush or spray the frozen dumplings all over with the oil. Do not thaw them first: thawed wrappers tear, stick to the basket and collapse.
Set the air fryer to 180°C, preheating only if your appliance manual requires it.
Arrange the dumplings flat side down in a single layer with gaps. Basket capacity depends on the model and dumpling size; divide into batches if needed rather than assuming 12 will fit.

Cook for 9 to 12 minutes, shaking or turning them at about 6 minutes, until the wrappers are golden and crisp at the edges and the filling is steaming hot the whole way through. The packet's own instructions are the authority for the product you actually bought; if one is still cool inside, give them 2 more minutes.

Oil does not guarantee that the wrappers will not stick. After cooking, switch off, unplug and let the appliance cool before cleaning. Follow its manual for removable parts, soaking and cleaning products; never immerse the electrical unit or assume water alone is enough.

yield_note: Twelve dumplings — a light meal for one, or a snack shared between two. About 12 minutes from freezer to plate. Editorial measuring convention for these original notes: tablespoon 20 mL; teaspoon 5 mL. These are volume measures, not gram conversions.

caveats: The packet is the authority for the product in your freezer. Fillings, wrapper thickness and pack sizes differ, and the manufacturer's instructions override anything written here.
Cook them from frozen and eat them hot. Do not part-cook dumplings and finish them off later.
These notes are written for vegetable dumplings. Meat and seafood fillings have their own requirements and their own packet instructions, and nothing here is guidance for them.
Allergens: wheat in the wrappers, and often soy, egg or sesame in the filling and the dipping sauce. All of it is on the packet.
These are practical notes: untested by this project, with no professional food-safety review.
